impact_pathways.impact_narrative: FIELDWISE builds the fellow's cross-disciplinary profile — biological understanding of water stress, scalable Sentinel-based geospatial prediction, and operational decision support (outcome OC6) — through the Career Development Plan (D1.3), agreed by M3 and reviewed at five steering points (M6, M12, M16, M20, M27), and through the inter-sectoral placement at AgroVIR. This directly advances the fellow's employability and career prospects within academia and beyond.

impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: expected_impacts.json EI-02; source_section 'Expected Outcome — For supported postdoctoral fellows'; HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01-01.slice.json
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The Hungary-to-Bulgaria transferability report produced with MVCRI (D4.2) supplies the international dimension; the AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation and non-academic placement (D5.4) supply the inter-sectoral dimension; and the two-way transfer between plant physiology and geoinformatics supplies the interdisciplinary dimension. Together these outputs, which realise the cross-country transferability outcome (OC3) and the field-level decision-value outcome (OC4), strengthen international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary research collaboration.

impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: expected_impacts.json EI-05; source_section 'Expected Outcome — For participating organisations'; HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01-01.slice.json
impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer are carried by three concrete transferable outputs: the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2), which realises the Sentinel-transferable early-warning feature basis (OC1); the released FIELDWISE predictive engine with its model card (D3.2), which realises the prospective forecasting capability (OC2); and the adaptation protocol (D4.3), which realises the quantified transferability outcome (OC3). Combined with the two-way transfer between the fellow and ELTE and the partner contributions of MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR, these outputs strengthen R&I capacity and knowledge transfer among European research organisations.

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: FIELDWISE follows Horizon Europe / MSCA open-science requirements: all peer-reviewed publications are made openly accessible; research data and the harmonised multi-season archive (D1.1) are curated to be FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable) with documented QC flags and metadata; the released predictive engine (D3.2) is accompanied by a published model card; and a Data Management Plan is delivered as a distinct deliverable by month 6 and updated periodically. Any data or feature exchange with MVCRI and AgroVIR respects agreed access conditions.

activities.activity_type: Advance the desktop research prototype to a scientifically validated web MVP serving stress probability, uncertainty, spatial risk, irrigation priority and temporal evolution (D5.1)
activities.expected_result: A reachable web MVP demonstrating operational water-stress decision support for processing tomato, validated by external AgroVIR evaluation
activities.timing: WP5, culminating in the AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation (D5.4)

activities.activity_type: Package the transfer library (D2.2), released predictive engine with model card (D3.2) and adaptation protocol (D4.3) as reusable assets for other agro-environments
activities.expected_result: A transferable early-warning feature basis and forecasting engine with a stated minimum local-calibration volume, reusable by European research organisations beyond the Hungary and Bulgaria test cases
activities.timing: On delivery of D2.2, D3.2 and D4.3 across WP2-WP4

activities.activity_type: Define the FMIS integration roadmap naming required interfaces and post-fellowship steps (D5.5)
activities.expected_result: A concrete path to embed FIELDWISE outputs into farm management information systems, informed by AgroVIR's assessment of actual agricultural software requirements

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: FIELDWISE has no explicit Tier 3 IPR data; as an MSCA postdoctoral fellowship the default position is background/results ownership by the host ELTE with the fellow as author-inventor, and open dissemination of scientific results (open-access publications, released transfer library, model card) as the primary route to impact. Where the web MVP or predictive engine has commercialisation potential, protection would rely primarily on copyright in the software and on trade secrets around calibration data, with any patenting considered only if the AgroVIR evaluation identifies protectable, novel technical subject matter; access and use of MVCRI and AgroVIR data are governed by the partners' agreed conditions.

sustainability_mechanism.description: FIELDWISE results persist beyond the fellowship through several concrete mechanisms: the released predictive engine and its model card (D3.2) and the harmonised multi-season archive (D1.1) remain maintained, FAIR research outputs held at ELTE; the transfer library (D2.2) and adaptation protocol (D4.3) provide a documented, reusable method — with a stated minimum local-calibration cost — for transferring the approach to further crops and regions; the FMIS integration roadmap (D5.5), grounded in AgroVIR's external evaluation, defines the post-fellowship steps required to move the validated web MVP toward operational use; and the co-designed ELTE MSc module unit embeds the project's methods into ongoing higher-education teaching, sustaining knowledge transfer into the next generation of researchers.
